findings.reason: Step 2.2 equates the event {S=r, X_{jL} not in A} with a future event that avoids A at every time. The latter is only a subset of the former, so the displayed equality is false; the lower bound needed for the contradiction follows with ≥. This remains unresolved on the final review.

Step 1.2 applies the invariant-drift lemma, whose statement requires a bounded drift set (sup_C V < infinity). The theorem assumes only a finite-valued V and small C, and does not derive that premise or pi V < infinity. The reduction proof constructs a bounded set with an improved drift, but the reduction statement does not expose that result and the theorem does not use it. Make this application explicit or supply the missing finite-moment result.

The approved BCS-32 design both defines drift pairs using globally finite V and describes the geometric theorem with V finite pi-almost everywhere. The current definition and theorem require global finiteness. If the a.e. clause permits infinite values on a pi-null set, that approved case is not covered; the owner should reconcile the intended scope.
